briefFidelity: FAIL, and the disagreement is total. The brief commissions ARCADE: repeated bays seen head on, a colonnade abstracted to interval and weight, the same member restated at different scale and NESTED INWARD, engineered and load-bearing, with ONE WARM ACCENT on the innermost bay. Before reading it I described these frames, unprompted, as a rosette, a mandala, a snowflake, a rose window and a shattered mosaic - the words colonnade, bay, column, span, support and interval never came near, because there is nothing linear or bay-like to see. Every seed (1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661, 1366079, 1475115, 1733538, 1835793) is a ROTATIONAL kaleidoscope: a cluster of translucent squares spun six- to eight-fold about the centre. Radial repetition is not a run of bays; a rose window is not a colonnade. Second, and independently fatal because it is a single named checkable element: there is NO warm accent anywhere - not in the innermost bay, not at the core, not in any of the twelve seeds nor in any of the twelve state frames. 1835793 and 1991107, whose cores are the most articulated and where the accent would have to live, are cold blue-slate. Third, the character is wrong: more than half of every frame is a scatter of squares tumbled at arbitrary angles (heaviest in 1366079, 1203347, 1985692), which reads as debris and confetti, the opposite of regular, load-bearing and slightly severe. Only the near-black ground and the iron/ash range match the brief.
composition: There is a real focal hierarchy in the mid-density seeds - 1310661 and 1475115 both set a clear pale ring against a large flat slate interior and let the surrounding scatter recede, and 1243682 holds a crisp six-pointed centre. But it is the SAME hierarchy twelve times: a centred medallion floating in the middle of the frame, with the frame itself used only as a crop for the debris rather than as a structure the work is built against. That is precisely the wrong compositional instinct for a colonnade, which lives in the run across the frame, not in a bullseye. Three seeds have no working hierarchy at all: 1985692 is a near white-out whose pale mass touches all four edges, 1991107 nearly the same, and 1446330 has no focal object whatsoever.
collectionCoherence: The strongest axis by a distance, arguably too strong. All twelve - 1203347 through 1991107 - share one element (the flat rotated translucent square), one staging (centred rosette inside a scatter field), one ground and one value range, so there is no doubt they are one project. Nothing here reads as a folder of unrelated frames. The cost is that coherence is delivered by literal repetition of a single generator rather than by a shared architectural idea, so 1203347, 1283437 and 1366079 feel like the same object photographed at three exposures.
palette: Chosen, and the best-executed part of the work: near-black ground around #16181a, cold slate mid-tones, bone-pale plates, no chroma competing with the drawing. The ground genuinely supports rather than fights - 1310661 and 1475115 use it as real negative space and the contrast range does work there. Two seeds waste it: 1985692 compresses everything into a narrow pale band with almost no internal contrast, and 1446330 sits so far down the scale it reads as an under-exposed render. And measured against the brief the palette is incomplete, not merely restrained: the one warm accent the brief names is absent from all twelve seeds and all twelve state frames, so the only colour decision that was specified is the one not taken.
seedVariation: The variation is of AMOUNT, not of kind - density, scale and overall value move, the idea never does. 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661 and 1366079 are one work at five densities; put side by side they differ mainly in how much black is left. The two ends overshoot into failure rather than into difference: 1446330 is so near-empty it reads as a broken token, and 1985692 is so full it reads as a blank pale field. The genuinely distinct frames are few - 1475115 (open slate annulus), 1561509 (small dark speckled cluster in a lot of black) and 1991107 (pale mass, dark speckled core). So the project is not too wide; it is too narrow in idea and too wide in exposure.
thumbnailSurvival: At 120 the silhouette survives - the rosette-on-black shape is legible on every seed and the outliers are instantly identifiable: 1446330 (near-empty), 1985692 (white-out), 1991107 (pale with dark core), 1561509 (small dark cluster), 1475115 and 1733538 (slate rings). But the five dense pale seeds collapse toward each other: 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661 and 1366079 all read as the same pale scalloped rosette with grey confetti, because the core detail that separates them at 256 is exactly what disappears at 120. Twelve tokens read as roughly six things. The fine speckle in the cores of 1835793, 1561509 and 1991107 turns to noise rather than detail at browse size.
marketResponse: This is the axis the work delivers, and it delivers it visibly at 120px, which is where it counts. Neutral is the fullest, palest, most consolidated state; STRESS genuinely fractures the medallion - 1203347 stress loses its ring entirely and becomes six or seven detached knots with ground showing between them, 1243682 stress opens a literal black pinhole at dead centre, 1283437 stress smears into a dark radial burst, and 1310661 stress inverts into a flat dark slate disc with a small pale star left behind. Read against the brief's words, members are lost and the interval widens, so the direction is right even though the subject is wrong. Recovery is the weak half: 1243682 recovery and 1243682 neutral are close to interchangeable at 120, and 1203347 recovery is nearly so, so the brief's claim that the nesting DEEPENS in recovery is not visible - recovery reads as a return to neutral, not as a state of its own.
tokenIdentity: Held, and held by a deliberate device: the surrounding scatter field does not move between states - the same large squares sit in the same places in the neutral, stress and recovery rows of 1203347, 1243682, 1283437 and 1310661 - so the token stays recognisable while the medallion carries the state. That is the right architecture for this. The one place it strains is 1310661, where stress inverts the value relationship (pale ring with dark core becomes dark disc with pale core); on that frame alone the subject is close to being replaced rather than stressed, and only the fixed surround keeps it the same token.
artifacts: Nothing broken, several things unhandled. Large scatter squares are cropped hard by the viewBox on all four sides of nearly every seed - 1203347, 1366079 and 1985692 worst - which reads as intentional bleed but leaves half-squares at the corners that look accidental in 1366079. In 1985692 and 1991107 the pale mass runs into the frame edge and the composition loses its ground entirely. The scatter overlaps and muddles the medallion outline in 1366079 and 1733538, so the two structures collide into grey mush instead of reading as figure and field. 1446330 is sparse enough to read as a rendering failure rather than a quiet token. Core speckle in 1835793, 1561509 and 1991107 sits at the resolution limit and degrades to noise at 120.
reasoning: REFUSE, decided at the gate and not on quality. On its own terms this is competent and in places good: the palette is disciplined, the collection is unmistakably one project, the stress state is a real and legible structural change at browse size, and token identity is protected by an intelligent choice to freeze the surround. But the commission was ARCADE - a colonnade flattened to interval and weight, bays nested inward, engineered and load-bearing, with one warm accent on the innermost bay - and what was made is a radially symmetric kaleidoscope rosette inside a field of tumbled debris, in a wholly achromatic palette. I wrote that description before I had read a word of the brief, and it contains no architectural noun at all; rotation is not rhythm, a rose window is not a run of bays, and the single specified colour event does not exist in any of the twenty-four frames I was shown. The market behaviour is right in direction and wrong in subject, which is the clearest statement of the problem: the mechanism was built well and pointed at another artwork. Failing this axis is not close, so the accomplishment elsewhere cannot carry it.
wouldChange: Rebuild the geometry on a linear register instead of a rotational one: replace the polar array with a set of concentric rectangular bays sharing the frame's axes - the same member restated at descending scale, nested inward, edges parallel and interval measurable - so that the eye reads span and support rather than spin. Kill the arbitrary rotation on the scatter entirely; a load-bearing structure cannot sit in confetti, so either align the field members to the same axes and let them become the outer bays, or remove them and let the near-black ground do the work it already does well in 1310661 and 1475115. Introduce the missing warm accent as a single low-chroma ember - ochre or oxide - occupying only the innermost bay, so it also becomes the focal anchor the centred compositions currently lack. Keep the state mechanism exactly as it is but re-express it as bays dropping out of the run and the interval widening under stress, and make recovery earn its own frame by adding a nesting level rather than returning to neutral, since 1243682 recovery and neutral are indistinguishable at 120. Finally bound the density range: 1446330 and 1985692 are outside anything that reads as the same work and should be clamped.
